author: Press Association
description:
• Ukrainian wins 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 after eight-minute timeout

  • ‘I tried to direct this anger towards the ball’

Elina Svitolina staged a remarkable comeback to beat Karolina Muchova and remain in the hunt for the WTA Finals title.

The Ukrainian looked to be on her way out of Indian Wells when she was a set down and required an eight-minute medical timeout. But she recovered to win 3-6, 6-2, 6-2 and stay in with a chance of reaching the semi-finals.

Continue reading...
title: Svitolina stays in WTA Finals hunt after remarkable fightback sees off Muchova

author: Adria R Walker
description:
Democrat chatted up people at hair salons, colleges and at Trump rallies to become Mississippi’s first Black senator since Reconstruction

The ad is simple, less than half a minute long, but many say it was the moment the nation took notice of Mississippi’s US Senate race.

In it, the incumbent Republican senator Cindy Hyde-Smith, a cattle farmer, answers a reporter’s question about the rising price of beef: “You know, you have so many proteins to choose from,” she says.

Continue reading...
title: How Scott Colom won deep-red Mississippi with little help from Democrats

author: Adria R Walker in Mississippi
description:
Colom takes victory by razor-thin margin in state that hasn’t elected a Democrat to the Senate since 1982

Democrat Scott Colom defeated Cindy Hyde-Smith, the incumbent Republican senator, to become the first Black senator in Mississippi elected since reconstruction, in a stunning upset after more than a week of vote counting in one of the country’s most reliably red states.

Colom opened up a narrow lead over Hyde-Smith late on election night. His lead widened as election officials counted provisional ballots. Hyde-Smith was not able to close the gap.

Continue reading...
title: Democrat Scott Colom unseats Cindy Hyde-Smith in shocking Mississippi Senate win

author: Guardian sport
description:
• Warriors star defends wife over romantic comedy role

  • Arenas called Ayesha ‘only blemish’ on Curry family

  • Four-time NBA champion condemns double standards

Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has criticized several ex-professional athletes for questioning his wife Ayesha’s decision to appear in a romantic comedy featuring an on-screen kiss, accusing them of diminishing her accomplishments and perpetuating double standards about women.

The four-time NBA champion posted a 90-second video on Instagram on Wednesday in response to comments by former NBA players Gilbert Arenas and Nick Young, as well as former NFL players Emmanuel Acho and LeSean McCoy, following the release of Ayesha Curry’s new film, Second Chance Holiday.

Continue reading...
title: Stephen Curry attacks treatment of women after former players criticize wife Ayesha’s movie kiss

author: Phil Harrison
description:
Inspired by the story of Maxine Carr, this twisty drama follows a group of women accused of helping a killer. It tackles everything from witch hunts to incel culture … and unravels like a real-life version of The Traitors

Hunting Alice Bell begins with a familiar scene. A woman has been found guilty of aiding and abetting Jason Nash (Simon Pegg), a murderous anaesthetist and also her former boyfriend. A furious crowd has gathered to bang on the van as it takes her away to serve 18 months in prison. But the woman under the blanket is a decoy – the real Alice Bell is being smuggled out of another exit. The mob’s bloodlust is deferred but not satisfied. Upon her release, Bell will be given a new identity.

Several years later, the life of Fran Da Silva (Alexandra Roach) is about to change for ever. She’s sitting down to breakfast with her husband and two teenage stepchildren when a brick crashes through the window. She’s ostracised at work. The kids come home
title: Hunting Alice Bell review – this conspiracy theory thriller starring Simon Pegg is a hot mess

author: Alexander Abnos
description:
• USSF cites state department advisory about Qatar

  • Competition set to kick off in eight days

The US men’s national team have pulled out of the Fifa U-17 World Cup, which is due to kick off in Qatar in just over a week. In a letter sent to players explaining the decision, the US Soccer Federation cited safety concerns for players and staff, referring them to the US state department’s travel advisory for Qatar, which encourages citizens to reconsider travel to the country “due to risk of armed conflict” and asks government employees to obtain special authorization to do so.

“Unfortunately, in light of current circumstances … we are no longer able to participate in the tournament,” US Soccer’s letter to players reads. “The wellbeing of our players and staff will always be our top priority.
title: US withdraw from U-17 World Cup in Qatar due to safety concerns

author: Owen Myers
description:
Once a Dallas school teacher, Hall became a star in later life with roles in Soul Food and Collateral

Actor Irma P Hall, star of Soul Food and the Coen brothers’ The Ladykillers, has died at the age of 91.

Hall died on Tuesday, her family confirmed alongside a statement that described her as “a beloved actress, author, poet, educator and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career”.

title: Veteran actor Irma P Hall, star of The Ladykillers, dies aged 91

The SS United States will sink off the coast of Destin, Florida to become an artificial reef, ending long-running wrangle over its fate

title: SS United States to be sunk to become the world’s largest artificial reef - watch live

author: David Batty and agency
description:
L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, from 4th Battalion of Royal Regiment of Scotland, charged with one count of rape on 23 October

A British soldier has been charged with the alleged rape of a UK army servicewoman in Cyprus.

L/Cpl Nicholas Horne, who serves in the 4th Battalion of the Royal Regiment of Scotland, also known as The Highlanders, was charged with one count of rape on 23 October, the Defence Serious Crime Command (DSCC) said.

Continue reading...
title: British soldier charged with rape of army servicewoman in Cyprus

author: AFP
description:
74-year-old Leonardo Bertulazzi, awaiting extradition to Italy, reportedly used harness to flee custody

A 74-year-old former member of Italy’s radical Marxist group the Red Brigades has escaped from house arrest in Argentina, the country’s security ministry confirmed on Wednesday.

Authorities placed Leonardo Bertulazzi under house arrest in Buenos Aires in 2024, prior to his extradition to Italy to serve a 27-year prison sentence.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-member of radical Marxist group scales balcony, escapes house arrest in Argentina

author: Ali Martin in Perth
description:
White-ball tour begins in Perth on Friday but there is only one story in Australian cricket and the tourists are not it

It feels like five minutes since England were last in pristine Perth, preparing – or rather under-preparing – to win back the Ashes, only for their glass jaw to be shattered by the flashing blade of Travis Head and a two-day defeat at Optus Stadium. But 12 months on, the mood is much changed.

Beyond the fact this is merely a white-ball tour – three one-day internationals starting on Friday, followed by five Twenty20s – England’s main character energy has seemingly evaporated. Brendon McCullum is still the head coach in limited-overs cricket but no one is talking about “Bazball” or trying to sell it as some kind of sequel.
title: England return to site of Ashes angst but Australia gaze stuck on sandpaper

author: David Hytner
description:
• Captain’s 126th cap against Croatia will top Shilton’s record

  • Kane aims to increase record for younger players to catch

Harry Kane says he still feels a pressure to prove his worth, even as he prepares to become England’s most capped men’s player, as he outlined his determination to set records that will stand for years.

The captain will make his 126th appearance against Croatia at ­Wembley on Thursday night, moving him ahead of Peter Shilton on the all-time list. Kane is England’s record ­goalscorer with 91, comfortably clear of Wayne Rooney, who retired with 53.

Continue reading...
title: ‘I’ve had to prove people wrong’: Kane still striving before record England cap

author: Paul MacInnes
description:
• It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll

  • Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’

A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino.

If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

Continue reading...
title: Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper

author: Oliver Milman, Fiona Harvey and Graham Readfearn in Antalya, and Ajit Niranjan
description:
Marshall Islands president warns of worsening floods as UN chief calls for a windfall tax on oil and gas firms

Failure to provide an overwhelming response to the climate crisis means “the world we know is over”, the president of the embattled Marshall Islands has warned, as dozens of leaders gathered in Turkey for the Cop31 climate summit.

Hilda Heine, one of a handful of Pacific Island leaders to make an impassioned speech at Cop31 on Wednesday, told other heads of state that overshooting the 1.5C Paris temperature target would mean waves eating away their shores and floods that destroy towns, schools and hospitals.

Continue reading...
title: ‘The world we know is over’ without urgent climate action, leaders tell Cop31

author: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic editor
description:
Regime adviser says Tehran could be forced into pre-emptive strikes if stalemate continues

Senior Iranian officials believe the US is planning either further military strikes or an ever-tightening economic stranglehold that will push Tehran into retaliatory action.

The assessment comes from Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

Continue reading...
title: Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials

author: Andrew Lawrence
description:
Incompetent direction almost kills the Christmas spirit but American Idol winner Fantasia Barrino Taylor brings down the house

Thanksgiving is right around the corner, which means Christmas creep is in full effect and the floodgates holding back the seasonal tide of holiday movies have opened to fully drown yuletide junkies in cheer. Among the first out of the gates is Netflix’s The Gospel of Christmas, brought to you by the maker of A Madea Christmas.

Instead of Tyler Perry in drag, reluctantly upholding the role of family linchpin, this time it’s Durrell Babbs – AKA the R&B stalwart Tank – playing Isaac, a secular musician who is forced into ministry when his pastor father charges him with resurrecting a sister congregation that’s become a blight in a New York neighborhood defined by immorality and anomie. (East New York, maybe.) The 103-minute feature is both a ploy to horn in on Hallmark’s well-established territory and a proper return to Perry’s roots
title: Tyler Perry’s The Gospel of Christmas review – Netflix unloads more slapdash festive fare

author: Presented by Lucy Hough with Devika Bhat ; produced by Angus Neale ; senior producer Leonore Schick ; executive producer Zoe Hitch
description:
Donald Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against the BBC has been granted permission to proceed, after the corporation’s attempt to get it dismissed was thrown out by a Trump-appointed Florida judge. The case focuses on an edit in a 2024 Panorama documentary that spliced two comments together that were made by the president during a rally before the January 6 Capitol riots, for which the BBC has apologised. With the lawsuit now set to continue, what’s at stake for press freedom? Lucy Hough speaks to global editor Devika Bhat

description:
Republicans know that the president’s folly and excesses cost them the elections. That doesn’t mean they’re ready to challenge him

Shortly after polls closed last Tuesday, with the scale of the Republican trouncing in the midterms still becoming apparent, Donald Trump briefly adopted an oddly conciliatory tone. He declared that he was “absolutely” willing to accept the results, would look forward to working with Democrats and that deportation policies might have been “too tough”.

title: The Guardian view on Maga after the midterms: doubling down on Trumpism | Editorial

author: Adam Sweeting
description:
American guitarist and songwriter who was a founding member of the punk band Television

When the New York band Television released their debut album Marquee Moon in February 1977, it provoked euphoria among critics, even if they were not quite sure how to describe it – punk, art-rock, new wave, post-punk, progressive or just rock were all terms flung in its direction.

It would frequently be described as an “influence” on countless acts who came after them, but Television’s music was too rare and sophisticated to be easily imitated, made as it was by a unique blend of musical personalities and instrumental skills.

Continue reading...
title: Richard Lloyd obituary

author: Adrian Chiles
description:
After Peta’s call ‘to reject mischaracterisations of chickens’, I wonder what they would make of Polish representations of polecats and Croatian cuckoos

Chickens don’t have it easy. On top of living largely crap, short lives, they endure the ignominy of collectively being a byword for cowardice. The campaign group People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) has written to the Oxford English Dictionary asking for this definition of “chicken” to be changed. Naturally enough, there are those who have been unafraid to holler “Woke nonsense!” as loud as cocks crowing.

For my part, I think Peta is right to stick up for chickens, but I’m not sure removing a definition – assuming definition-removal is a thing – would make any difference. Chicken, in this sense, is in common use as an adjective, a verb and a noun. It’s got deep roots that are going to take some shifting. And any such move could open up a right can of worms (sorry, worms). What about the vulture, rat, shar
title: Chickens are synonymous with cowardice. Is it time to stick up for our feathered friends? | Adrian Chiles

ESPN analyst and former NFL coach Rex Ryan turned himself in to police on Wednesday after allegedly hitting two pedestrians with his car in Nashville and leaving the scene.

Nashville police said on Wednesday that the pedestrians had the right of way while crossing a main street in the city’s downtown last week when Ryan allegedly turned at a red light and drove over their feet.

author: Emma Brockes
description:
He has survived blame for the US midterms disaster and dodged an impeachment vote, but it will be one battle after another now – and he can’t win them all

Like the brief, wondrous cycle of the mayfly, we may come to look back on the career of Pete Hegseth, the US secretary of defence who cheekily rebranded himself secretary of war, as the defining appointment of the Trump era: that is, one in which extraordinary power was handed to a man of cartoonish inappropriateness and which, despite this week’s shelved attempt to impeach him, may still turn out to have been luminously short-lived. In January, the Democrats will assume a majority in both chambers and are likely to have another crack at impeaching Hegseth. In the meantime, we can only look on and wonder at his meaning.

It is quite something, in the context of Trump cabinet appointments that have included Robert F Kennedy Jr and
title: Why does Pete Hegseth call himself secretary of war? ‘Dopey but dangerous’ wouldn’t fit on a badge | Emma Brockes

author: Ronald Bergan
description:
Versatile American stage and screen actor whose roles ranged from Hamlet to the tough private eye Mike Hammer

There have been few actors as inexhaustible as Stacy Keach, who has died aged 85. Throughout a long career that began in his childhood he was equally active in theatre, films and TV, moving from the sublime to the ridiculous and back again with aplomb. Perhaps it was his ubiquity and eclecticism that caused him to be so underrated.

Keach meant different things to different people. To theatregoers, he was a fine Shakespearean actor, acclaimed for his Hamlet, who was also adept in other classics and musicals (Barnum, Camelot, The King and I). To the filmgoer, he was one of the faces of Hollywood in the 1970s. To the television viewer, Keach was the tough private eye Mike Hammer, in the 80s TV series and spinoffs based on the novels by Mickey Spillane.
title: Stacy Keach obituary

Lisa Nandy expected to meet leaders from television, film and publishing and could legislate if voluntary action deemed insufficient

Ministers are considering changing the law to force the entertainment industry to better protect women and children in the wake of the revelations over David Walliams and the conviction of Russell Brand.

Lisa Nandy, the culture secretary, is expected to meet leaders from the industry next week, taking in representatives from not just TV but also film and publishing, as well as potentially sport.

title: Ministers consider forcing TV industry to better protect women after David Walliams allegations

description:
US envoys to visit Moscow and Dublin on Thursday for talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy respectively

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to the “largest prisoner exchange” of the war at their first US-brokered talks since February but made little progress towards a broader peace agreement.

Both sides sent senior delegations to the two-day talks, led by Donald Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, in an effort to find a solution to end the nearly-five-year war.

title: Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi bring progress on prisoners but not on peace

author: Arwa Mahdawi
description:
Trump has already made history as the only president to be impeached twice. After the Republicans’ thrashing in the midterms, could there be a third attempt?

The days are getting shorter, the nights are getting longer and some Republicans are getting nervous. After a long stretch of impunity, it’s impeachment season in the US. While the attempt to impeach the defence secretary, Pete Hegseth, failed yesterday, Donald Trump may be worried he’s next.

In January, the president warned Republicans that they had better win the November elections or he would be in big trouble. “If we don’t win the midterms … they’ll find a reason to impeach me,” Trump said. He repeated this plea to voters during an
title: It’s impeachment season! After the attempt on Pete Hegseth, will Donald Trump be next? | Arwa Mahdawi

author: Robert Kitson
description:
Japan head coach was criticised for discarding players harshly during his Red Rose tenure but that tough love has paid off for some

To listen to Eddie Jones chewing the fat on assorted podcasts this week is to admire the enduring thickness of his coaching skin. The old crocodile smile is still intact too, along with his sense of humour after an interaction in a lift with a fan after his Japan side’s 28-21 weekend defeat in Cardiff. As Jones later confided: “This Welsh bloke came up to me and said: ‘You almost look human with your glasses on.’”

Next up is a reunion with a few former friends – and foes – in Twickenham. While it is now almost four years since Jones was sacked by the Rugby Football Union, there remain mixed emotions on both sides.
title: Eddie Jones retains his passion and divisive power heading into England reunion

author: Madeleine Aggeler
description:
Slow blinking and trilling are some of the ways felines show affection – but experts say to ‘read the whole cat in context’

I talk to my cat, Blue, constantly. I say things like, “You’re my little baby,” and “Wow, good jump,” and “Can you stop being a jerk for like, two seconds?”

She also seems to say a lot, like, “Feed me,” “Feed me right now,” and “Stop working and play with me.”

author: Benjamin Lee
description:
Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai and Pete Davidson play Robin Hood in this simple-minded and unexciting attempt to mix social commentary with action

In case you were somehow blissfully unaware, America is in a very dark place and Americans are not very happy about it. Last week’s midterms saw a historic blue wave propelled by the high cost of living and the low trust in those making decisions, but restoring any small shred of faith in the system and any vague semblance of financial equity is still unlikely to come any time soon.

It’s therefore theoretically ideal timing for films that provide some sort of rousing David v Goliath catharsis, a win on-screen when one feels entirely out of reach in real life. author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
description:
Departure of Tom Waterhouse, Reform’s ‘latest fall guy’, will be blow to party amid push towards professionalisation

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Reform UK’s general secretary has left the role as Nigel Farage’s party continues to face turmoil over questions about vetting failures and professionalisation.

The departure of Tom Waterhouse comes after Reform UK’s leader on Hampshire county council, George Madgwick, was charged with 12 counts of rape and one of distributing indecent images of a child.

Continue reading...
title: Senior Reform UK official quits as questions over vetting failures continue

author: Ella Creamer
description:
Kazuo Ishiguro, Jeff VanderMeer, Olivia Laing and other writers weigh in on the publishing world’s genre wars

As M John Harrison was announced as the Booker prize winner on Monday evening, the 81-year-old looked gobsmacked. Decades into his career, and long overlooked by the mainstream literary establishment, he had just won a prize that has never before rewarded a writer known for science fiction, with a decidedly fantastical book.

His fans, many leading authors among them, are thrilled. “For decades it was a standard – and correct – nerd whine to point out that sentence for sentence, book for book, Harrison was one of the greatest writers out there, full stop, but that ‘mainstream’ prizes never reflected that,” says China Miéville, who last week won the Goldsmiths prize with his 1,200-page speculative novel

description:
Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes

  • US politics live – latest updates

Democratic lawmakers expressed outrage at nearly a dozen of their colleagues for missing a vote Tuesday evening to impeach the defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, allowing Republicans to squash the effort.

Eleven Democrats missed the key procedural vote on the impeachment effort, which failed by just seven votes. Some blamed traffic and conflicting events and others accused Speaker Mike Johnson of closing the vote early. Many of those not i

author: Daniel Boffey in Hamburg
description:
Lawyer says Britain wrong to believe in historic doctrine that crown has sovereignty over parts of oceans

Britain should not be permitted to act as a 17th-century colonial power treating the waters around the Falkland Islands as a Dominium maris Britannici, Argentina has told an international tribunal.

Marcelo Kohen, representing Argentina at a hearing in Hamburg, mocked Britain for apparently believing in the historic doctrine that the British crown has sovereignty over expansive parts of the oceans.

Continue reading...
title: Argentinian lawyer mocks UK’s sovereignty claim in Falklands oil case

author: Tom Garry
description:
• Team must win World Cup group to trigger rule

  • Spain, US, Germany and England currently in top four

The top four-ranked teams will be separated until the semi-finals at the 2027 Women’s World Cup, provided they each win their group, after a change to the tournament’s draw procedure was confirmed by Fifa.

Spain, the United States, Germany and England are currently ranked one to four in the world respectively, although the US and England still need to qualify for the tournament. The seedings will be based on 7 December’s updated rankings, meaning the standings could change before the draw, which will take place on 11 December in Rio de Janeiro.

Continue reading...
title: Top four teams in Fifa rankings set to be kept apart until semi-finals at 2027 Women’s World Cup

author: Kiran StaceyPolicy editor
description:
Exclusive: Cutting 2030 goal would be a ‘step backwards’, say MPs, as ministers clash over proposed reductions

  • UK politics live – latest updates

  • Cop31 live – latest updates

Labour MPs are urging the government not to weaken its electric vehicle targets as divided cabinet ministers prepare for a crunch meeting on Thursday to thrash out a compromise.

Members of the climate and nature crisis caucus (CNCC) say ministers must not water down a legal requirement for carmakers to ensure that 80% of the vehicles they sell in 2030 are electric, saying doing so would be a backward step and “shortsighted”.
title: Labour MPs warn against weakening electric vehicle targets ahead of crunch talks

author: Ian Sample Science editor
description:
Combining body mass index with other measurements and tests would lead to better care and outcomes, experts say

An alternative to BMI for diagnosing obesity could prevent misdiagnosis in millions of people worldwide, according to doctors who found it more accurately distinguished healthy people from those with harmful excess body fat.

Medical experts have long considered body mass index a blunt instrument for defining obesity, leading to concerns that substantial numbers of people with excess body fat are missed while others who are healthy are wrongly diagnosed.

title: BMI alternative for identifying obesity ‘could prevent misdiagnosis in millions’

author: Panashe Nyadundu
description:
Crystal Palace FC or Oxbridge beckoned, but the multitalented MC kept forging her way towards music. She explains how she poured every aspect of herself into her debut mixtape

Two weeks before we meet, UK rapper Cristale was scrambling down a cliff face to a secluded black pebbled beach in Dover, racing an incoming tide with fewer than 90 minutes to shoot the video for her single I’m Okay With Being Lonely. She’d never hiked before in her life. “I was wearing head-to-toe Stone Island, no hiking gear, full face of makeup, edges laid and Mum was doing my touch-ups on a rusty ladder,” she laughs.

As we sit in her publicist’s central London office, her hair half-braided and half-flowing past a black puffer coat, she says the rush of adrenaline hasn’t fully faded. author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
description:
Police assure parents and teachers that warnings were bogus despite pupils being evacuated from some sites

Hundreds of schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland were hit by a fresh wave of hoax bomb threats on Wednesday, with some sites evacuated as a precaution.

Police said at least 470 schools, from Dumfries in the south of Scotland to Aberdeenshire and Orkney in the north, had received the hoax warnings. At least 300 schools were affected in Northern Ireland. Similar claims were sent in a “generic communication” to schools in the Republic of Ireland.

Continue reading...
title: Hoax bomb threats made to hundreds of schools in Scotland and Northern Ireland

author: Interview by Charlotte Jansen
description:
‘I was chosen to go around the Moon on a SpaceX starship. Preparations took over my life. Then, four minutes into watching a rocket on a test flight, it broke apart. And that was the end of my adventure’

author: Owen Myers
description:
The California festival has unveiled its lineup, which also features Madonna, Phoebe Bridgers and Robyn

The lineup for the 2027 Coachella festival has been revealed after months of speculation, with Dua Lipa, SZA and Tame Impala set to headline the California event.

description:

This week my Instagram feed has been full of female friends, colleagues and acquaintances sharing his words: “Whatever women wear, wherever they go, indeed whatever they drink, they retain the right to say no and to demand justice from the criminal courts when sexual predators like you, Russell Brand, act without their consent.” Those same women are now sharing the Guardian and ITV’s
title: Why did it take so long to unmask Brand and Walliams? Because noughties culture told girls like me abuse was normal | Rhiannon Lucy Cosslett

author: Greg Wood
description:
• O’Brien rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps

  • ‘Tom meant so much to so many people across our sport’

Tom O’Brien, who rode more than 1,000 winners over jumps including five Grade Ones and two at the Cheltenham festival, has died at the age of 39 after being diagnosed with cancer.

O’Brien, who retired from race riding in April 2023, had a close association with Philip Hobbs’s stable near Minehead throughout his 20-year career in the saddle and enjoyed his most prestigious Grade One victories aboard Hobbs’s Thyme Hill in the Stayers’ Hurdle at Aintree in April 2021 and the Kauto Star Novice Chase at Kempton in December 2022.

author: Peter Bradshaw

I thought I knew what writing was: the solitude, the making yourself do it, the finger-shattering pain of doing it seriously, on your own.

As well as being chief film critic for the Guardian, I have written fiction and in some ways the basic technical challenge has not been so very different from cinema criticism; after having had the idea, or having seen the film, you have to go away on your own and turn the computer on.

They got engaged last year and will be married in September. Their days hum with the constant buzz of wedding planning: picking vendors, writing the guest list, dress shopping. Amos, who is 30, understands the concept has baggage. author: Amy Fleming
description:
One in five people have experienced this frightening state – and the Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal has dedicated his career to studying it. Could it be a portal to a deeper understanding of the mind?

The Harvard neuroscientist Baland Jalal is considering the unfathomable depths of the human brain. “It can contemplate itself, and vast galaxies, spirits, souls, poetry, Einstein. Yet you hold it in your hand and it seems so trivial.” Jalal’s passion – the subject that drove him to become a scientist – is sleep paralysis, a brain glitch that can fill its host with terror so palpable that it can cause lasting trauma. “What you get very close to in sleep paralysis,” he says, “is that subjective world of the mind. It’s very hard to put into words.”

He should know – he’s spent 271 pages trying to do so. His new book, The Phantom Mind, argues that by exploring the borderlands of sleep, where sleep paralysis occurs, we can delve deeper into how all aspects of our minds work

A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that tim
title: Which football club has had most international captains in the same team? | The Knowledge

author: Andrew Beasley
description:
While No 9s still score the most goals and No 1s try to stop them, trends have changed since the introduction of squad numbers in the early 1990s

How much is a shirt number worth? It costs £8 if you want two digits added to the back of Arsenal’s 2026-27 home shirt, whereas Manchester City add on £16 for customisation, whether you want a name as well as a number or not.

That is cheap compared to what baseball players decide among themselves. Juan Soto bought Brett Baty a $92,000 (£69,000) car in exchange for getting his preferred number (22) when he joined the New York Mets last year. But that’s baseball, where they allow players to wear ‘0’. Anything goes.

Continue reading...
title: Is No 10 still the best, or No 41? The myths and maths of Premier League shirt numbers

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Colin McPherson has spent three decades working on Catching the Tide, his moving portrayal of fishers and an old way of life that is dying out

Continue reading...
title: Back of the net! Scotland’s historic salmon fishers – in pictures

author: Annabelle Thorpe
description:
Saunas, seal-watching and spectacular skies feature in our picks of great places for a short break to enjoy winter in the raw. Plus boltholes to cosy up in

A murmuration of starlings is one of winter’s most mesmerising spectacles; thousands of birds, swooping in formation, before communally roosting to stave off the winter. Piers are a favourite place to roost, with up to 50,000 zooming around in the skies above Aberystwyth, best seen on an afternoon stroll along the prom. The town is also home to the National Library of Wales which is well worth a visit, both for its excellent gift shop and the chance to browse a few of the 8 million books and periodicals within its walls. Y Ffarmers, which is a few miles out of town, is excellent for a long lunch, and Gwesty Cymru, on the seafront, has doubles from £140 B&B.
title: 10 of the best wild winter weekends in the UK

author: Fiona Harvey in Antalya
description:
Many governments are yet to set targets, leaving recipient countries struggling to plan and attract private investment

Developing countries have been left in limbo by the failure of some of the world’s biggest economies to flesh out their plans for new climate finance.

Poor countries are supposed to receive $300bn a year from the governments of industrialised nations by 2035, along with about $1tn from other sources, to help them cope with the effects of extreme weather and shift to a low-carbon future.

Continue reading...
title: Developing countries in limbo as rich nations delay new climate finance plans

author: Rafael Behr
description:
A lesson from the US midterms is that electorates are repelled by the arrogant mega-rich buying democracy. This is a fight Labour can afford to pick

For most people, $224m (£168m) is a lot of money, especially if you spend it and get nothing in return. But Elon Musk is richer than most people. In fact, there is no one richer.

As the wealthiest of the US’s tech oligarchs Musk could afford to blow huge sums on a failed bid to prop up Republican candidates in Texas, his adoptive home state, in last week’s midterm congressional elections. He is reported to have spent a further $250m failing to engineer results in other races.

Rafael Behr is a Guardian columnist
title: For Trump, Musk and Farage, the message is the same: voters don’t want to be hijacked by billionaires | Rafael Behr

author: Rachel Clarke
description:
The data journalist puts her own finances – and those of ten others from across the economic spectrum – under a microscope

How much do you earn? If the question makes you bristle – and I realise we haven’t even met – would you answer it if someone convinced you that your candour might just change the world?

In her deliciously original first book, the former Guardian data journalist and illustrator Mona Chalabi sets out to do precisely that. The result – a dazzling mix of journalism, data visualisation and memoir – is both a joy to read and a serious provocation. Chalabi takes aim at our silence and furtiveness around individual income and finances. “Our collective ignorance is sustaining an unfair system,” she argues. Unless we talk more openly about our personal wealth, we will never be able to tackle the economic problems causing insecurity and anxiety for us all.
title: Ten Lives by Mona Chalabi review – what if we were totally honest about our wealth?

author: Deepa Parent
description:
Rights groups condemn reported punishment of Kenyan migrant worker as an ‘act of violence’

A Kenyan mother in Saudi Arabia has reportedly been sentenced to 100 lashes after giving birth outside marriage.

Under the Saudi sharia law system, sex outside marriage is a criminal offence. But it is women who are disproportionately targeted, say rights groups, which have condemned the punishment as an “act of violence”.

Continue reading...
title: Woman in Saudi Arabia sentenced to 100 lashes for giving birth outside marriage

author: Stephen Moss
description:
Forget the hoopoes and the ring-necked parakeets, the highlight of our trip was a sound I hadn’t heard for 50 years

As dusk falls on a warm October evening, I gradually become aware of a strange, high-pitched sizzling noise. From our table outside a busy bar, with Spaniards celebrating their national holiday, it reminds me of water carelessly tossed into a scorching frying pan.

I approach a bougainvillea bush decked with rich purple flowers, and the collective clamour separates into distinct notes. I realise I am listening to hundreds – perhaps thousands – of house sparrows, each bird calling frantically to their companions as they gather to roost for the night. It’s a sound I haven’t heard for more than 50 years.

Continue reading...
title: Humble house sparrows roosting in Spain evoke a childhood memory

author: George Monbiot
description:
The transition to electric vehicles should be moving apace, but it is not. And why? Incompetence, expedience and cowardice

This is how it works. An industry puts tremendous effort into resisting change: lobbying governments, mobilising the media, pouring money into junktanks. It argues that a transition would threaten jobs, or damage the national interest, or harm poor people, while what it really fears is the cost of retooling its plants or developing new protocols. Then, when the inevitable cliff edge approaches, it whines that change is coming too soon. For reasons beyond its control, it isn’t ready, so the government must delay its plans.

This is what triggered the Dutch
title: Why are Britain's streets still so polluted? Because the car industry dinosaurs do what they like, and politicians let them | George Monbiot

author: Kiran StaceyPolicy editor
description:
Exclusive: Reindustrialisation Research Group to meet with Cabinet Office to discuss worries over PM’s long-term strategy

Labour MPs have sounded the alarm over Andy Burnham’s 10-year plan for government, raising concerns that it will not be radical or detailed enough.

MPs in the Reindustrialisation Research Group (ReRG), many of whom represent “red wall” seats that helped Labour win the last election, are meeting Sally Jameson, the Cabinet Office minister, on Wednesday to share their concerns about the prime minister’s long-term strategy.

Continue reading...
title: Labour MPs raise concerns Burnham’s 10-year-plan will not be radical enough

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Homes in the West End, Mayfair and Marylebone are going unsold – and developers are counting the cost

London has no shortage of luxury flats. There are ultra-modern blocks in the most upmarket neighbourhoods – including Chelsea, Kensington and Mayfair – that offer marble lobbies, concierge services and views across the city’s skyline.

The problem for property developers is finding wealthy residents to fill them, leaving brand-new properties in London’s most desirable postcodes standing empty.

Continue reading...
title: Prime property, slow sales: why London’s stock of empty high-end flats is piling up

author: Guardian staff and Reuters
description:
Koah was found ‘clinging to life’ in a shallow grave after he went missing while in the care of his father, Lexington sheriff’s department said

An 11-month-old boy was found alive in South ⁠Carolina after he was believed to have been buried for ⁠about 24 hours, local police said.

The infant, Koah Sharpe, was found on Tuesday wrapped inside ⁠a dog crate that was in turn wrapped in a towel and buried just under the surface in the woods, according to the ​Lexington county sheriff’s department.

Continue reading...
title: Baby found alive after being buried in dog crate for 24 hours, South Carolina police say

author: Presented by Reged Ahmad and Jonathan Yerushalmy; produced by Lu Hill who also did the sound design and mixing; video production Rachel Herron; executive producer is Hannah Parkes
description:
Jonathan Yerushalmy and Reged Ahmad examine the Democrats’ failed impeachment attempt against the US defense secretary, Pete Hegseth, and ask: could we see another bid soon?

The other Donald Trump appointee making headlines is the president’s new chief of staff, Stephen Miller. Known as the architect of Trump’s tough immigration policies, the appointment is seen as a clear sign the president has no intention of playing nice with the other side, despite indicating he would do just that after the Republicans’ massive midterms loss. Jonathan looks back at Miller’s past to try and decipher how the descendant of a family fleeing persecution developed such hardline views that he has been condemned as a white nationalist

Read more:

House Republicans block effort to impeach Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth
title: Who is Stephen Miller, the new gateway man to Trump - podcast

author: First Dog on the Moon
description:
Is it because a) live music is just too hard (expensive) to do and b) AI streaming algorithms are eating our brains? Probably

  • Sign up here to get an email whenever First Dog cartoons are published

  • Get all your needs met at the First Dog shop if what you need is First Dog merchandise and prints

title: Australians are not streaming Australian music. Why the hell not?! | First Dog on the Moon

author: Kate Lamb
description:
Capture of man from Java follows reports that hundreds are being recruited from the south-east Asian country as Moscow seeks to boost its war effort

Ukraine says it has captured its first Indonesian prisoner of war, amid what it says is a spike in recruitment by Russia from the south-east Asian nation.

The 49-year-old man from Java was taken to Ukraine’s Zaporizhzhia region to take part in a Russian assault, but managed to reach Ukrainian-held territory after the group came under drone attack, according to Ukraine’s state-run I Want to Live project. He was then captured by the Ukrainians.

Continue reading...
title: Ukraine captures first Indonesian prisoner of war amid surge in Russian recruitment

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Conservationists relocate 3,400 one-flowered wintergreens, a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years

Thousands of one of Britain’s rarest wildflowers have been moved to safety from an eroding Scottish shoreline where they were at risk of falling into the sea.

Conservationists rescued 3,400 one-flowered wintergreen plants at Culbin Forest in Moray, in an effort to protect a species estimated to have lost more than half its UK population in the past 50 years.

Continue reading...
title: Thousands of rare wildflowers rescued from eroding Scottish coast

author: Miloš Hroch
description:
A new book, With Wittgenstein in a Gay Sauna, reveals the deep-rooted queer subcultures in cities from Budapest to Prague – defying regional stereotypes and inspiring an art exhibition on masculinity

The philosopher Ludwig Wittgenstein argued that our understanding of reality is fundamentally bound by and shaped by the language we use to talk about it. But there is one place where the Vienna-born thinker’s argument ceases to make sense. “Gay saunas are spaces where language dies,” says Vratislav Maňák, a Czech writer and literary scholar.

With Wittgenstein in a Gay Sauna, a book that made a major splash when it was published in Czech and German earlier this year, Maňák fictionalises Wittgenstein, who had romantic relations with both men and women, entering a Viennese Herrensauna called Kaiserbründl, hailed in newspapers at the time as “the most stylish bathing establis
title: ‘Homosexuality was coined by a Hungarian’: the gay-sauna travelogue questioning central Europe’s illiberal image

author: Graeme Virtue
description:
They’ve sidelined the harfoots, introduced a Stranger Things star and thrown in full-blooded romance. It’s probably not enough to stop the fantasy prequel feeling boring, though

It might seem strange to characterise the leading streaming show from one of the most dominant corporations on the planet as a scrappy underdog. But after a lavish-but-dramatically stilted debut in 2022 and a similarly well-heeled but darker second season in 2024, it does feel like prequel series The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power is somehow stuck on the back foot.

For all its finely wrought art dire
title: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season three review – this dull show’s revamp is too little, too late

author: Paul Taylor
description:
A deal giving Moscow a slice of Ukrainian territory and sanctions relief could be on the table in weeks – yet European leaders are busy squabbling

Donald Trump has lost substantial power over domestic policy after last week’s devastating midterm losses, but his ability to cement his legacy by upending US foreign policy remains largely intact.

There is every reason to fear a ”great betrayal” of Ukraine in the coming weeks, one that would reward Vladimir Putin for Russia’s war of aggression against Kyiv, and also do lasting damage to the European security order. Yet lilliputian European leaders are too busy squabbling over who should represent them in future peace talks to focus on how to prevent a sellout. Despite fundamental European interests being at
title: Trump could be about to sell out Ukraine. Europe must get its act together, fast | Paul Taylor

author: Lisa Allardice
description:
He is a sci-fi titan but M John Harrison has just exploded into the mainstream – with The End of Everything, an apocalyptic novel set on the Kent coast. Does he really think we have no hope left?

With his twinkling eyes and silver ponytail, M John Harrison doesn’t seem anything like his 81 years. The M stands for Michael, Mike to his friends. And last night he became the oldest author to win the Booker prize for fiction, for his 13th novel, The End of Everything. Our interview is delayed because of wifi issues, which is fitting given that the novel is about – among many things – what happens when non-human intelligence takes over.

The End of Everything is the first sci-fi novel to have won the prize in its 58-year history, which is almost as long as Harrison has been writing. “It’s interesting,” he replies, when asked if he feels vindicated, “that something that has an SF-adjacent feel can be regarded as a serious book and given the Booker prize. My problem has always b
title: ‘We are dream-walking into a desperate situation’: the Booker prize winner on his sci-fi alien invasion wakeup call

author: Lorenzo Tondo
description:
Independent Israeli professor says Hussam Abu Safiya’s life will be at risk until he receives proper medical treatment

An independent professor who reviewed the medical records of a prominent Gaza doctor held in an Israeli prison without charge for nearly 23 months has raised serious concerns about his health.

Hussam Abu Safiya was detained at work on 27 December 2024 and later held in solitary confinement at Rakefet, a notorious underground prison.

Continue reading...
title: Fresh concerns raised over Gaza doctor held by Israel for 23 months without charge

author: Anita Chaudhuri
description:
Almost two-thirds of bedfellows disagree about the perfect room temperature – and the issue can affect office workers and housemates too. It oftens lead to subterfuge and skulduggery. So is there any way to reach a truce?

Recently I read an item on Threads that made me laugh out loud. “New dating app idea: post your thermostat settings to find your match.” The poster then revealed their own preferences: a balmy 24C by day and a chilly 19C at bedtime.

The suggestion elicited a rush of responses. “As someone who married outside their thermostat bracket, all I can say is that this is the most brilliant idea ever,” enthused one user. “Get outta here with that daytime terrarium,” responded another. “Are you storing pallets of produce in your house that you need to keep cold?” chimed in a third.
title: The thermostat wars tearing couples apart: ‘It’s hard to feel sexy when you’re freezing cold’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Women are reportedly upstairs neighbors of three Black students, including one who uploaded video to TikTok

Two white students at the University of Mississippi were captured making offensive monkey gestures in a widely panned Ring video that has prompted a school investigation.

On Saturday, freshman Jakiyra Metcalf uploaded the surveillance clip from her apartment door to TikTok, showing one woman thumping her chest and babbling like a monkey. Another woman jumped into the camera’s view and mimicked the primate noises.

Continue reading...
title: Two white students at University of Mississippi make monkey gestures in Ring video

author: Associated Press
description:
The US actor died in Poland on Tuesday, ‘after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure’, his wife said

Stacy Keach, one of America’s finest stage actors who became best known for playing scruffy private eye Mike Hammer on TV and whose career was nearly derailed after he was imprisoned in 1984 for trying to smuggle cocaine into Britain, has died aged 85.

Keach died at home in Magdalenka, Poland on Tuesday, “after a long and difficult battle with a serious heart condition and heart failure,” his wife, Malgosia Tomassi Keach, said in a statement. Keach had previously suffered a heart attack onstage in Chicago in 2017.

Continue reading...
title: Stacy Keach, Mike Hammer actor whose career spanned stage and screen, dies aged 85

author: Jonathan Horn
description:
The interminable sandpaper scandal will drag on to the next press conference, social media post or book, until it festers into something much bigger than it needs to be

There are some stories that you look back on and wonder whether we lost our collective minds. In Australia, 2018 was not a good year for banking executives, for prime ministers, for oily lord mayors and for cardinals. But the greatest betrayal of trust apparently concerned our national cricket team. There was public bawling, righteous indignation, weasel words and sanctimonious pieties. Prime minister Malcolm Turnbull, flanked by a doleful Angus Taylor and a nodding firefighter, called it a “terrible disgrace”. “They now have to make sure this great national game, this great international game that is synonymous with fair play, is once again played by champions that everybody can look up to.”

Turnbull was more of a sailing man anyway. His parliamentary tenure was the political equivalent of Graeme Hick’
title: Cricket Australia wants to move on from ball tampering saga but its equivocation has the opposite effect | Jonathan Horn

author: Jamie Grierson
description:
Trusty Olivetti machine named ‘Monica 2’ was used for writer’s racy Rutshire chronicles

One of Jilly Cooper’s beloved manual typewriters – used to write her bestselling, scandal-filled Rutshire chronicles – is to go under the hammer at auction.

The Olivetti Underwood Lettera 32, which has a guide price of £10,000 to £15,000, was affectionately known by the late author as Monica 2.

Continue reading...
title: Jilly Cooper’s beloved typewriter could fetch £15,000 at auction

author: Phillip Inman
description:
Thinktank Niesr says timid rate rise last week likely to make inflation more persistent feature of UK economy

The Bank of England is risking higher interest rates for longer after a hesitant response to rising inflation, according to leading thinktank.

In a searing critique of the central bank’s tactics, the National Institute of Economic and Social Research (Niesr) said a timid increase in interest rates last week was likely to mean inflation staying above the Bank’s 2% target until at least 2030.

Continue reading...
title: Bank of England’s inflation response ‘risks higher interest rates for longer’

author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
description:
Ombudsman’s report says delays have profound consequences and limit users’ ability to lead independent lives

Disabled people are having to wait up to two years to get a wheelchair because of delays involving NHS bodies and private firms that make them.

The situation is revealed in a report by the parliamentary and health service ombudsman for England, Paula Sussex, who said hold-ups were having profound consequences and limiting wheelchair users’ ability to lead independent lives.

Continue reading...
title: Disabled people in England ‘have to wait up to two years for wheelchairs’
